draft.title: Protein
card: Protein is a nutrient the body uses to build and repair tissue, such as muscle, skin and organs. This is why growing children and people recovering from injury need enough of it.
The body also uses protein to make enzymes and hormones. Enzymes speed up chemical reactions such as digestion. Hormones are chemical messengers that carry signals around the body.
Animal foods that give protein include meat, fish, eggs and dairy foods such as milk, cheese and yoghurt.
Plant foods that give protein include legumes (such as lentils, chickpeas and beans) and nuts.
draft.remember: Protein builds and repairs the body and makes enzymes and hormones.

a.q: Jarrah tears a muscle playing football. Which job of protein helps the muscle heal?
opts: Building and repairing tissue
Making hormones to carry signals
Speeding up digestion with enzymes
Giving the body its main source of energy
a.why: Muscle is body tissue, and protein is used to repair it. Making hormones is a real job of protein, but hormones carry signals and do not rebuild damaged muscle.
a.clue: Think about what a torn muscle is made of.

b.q: Priya eats no meat, fish, eggs or dairy foods. Which meal would give her protein?
opts: Lentil soup with a handful of almonds
Fruit salad with a glass of juice
Plain white rice with steamed carrots
Toast with jam and a cup of black tea
b.why: Lentils are legumes and almonds are nuts, and both are plant sources of protein. The other meals are mostly fruit, grains and vegetables, which are not the protein foods named on the card.
b.clue: Look for a legume and a nut.

b.best: Lentil soup with a handful of almonds

problems.detail: 'Which meal would give her protein?' is loose: bread (toast) and even white rice contain some protein, so other options technically give protein. Rewording to 'the most protein' or 'a good source of protein' would remove the ambiguity.
